title: What meter interference can tell us about the statistics of weak measurements
authors: Holger F. Hofmann, Tomonori Matsushita, Masayoshi Isobe, Jonte R. Hance
abstract: It is widely assumed that the quantum fluctuations of the meter readout in a weak measurement make it impossible to identify the contributions originating from the individual values of the physical property observed in the measurement. Here, we show that a careful analysis of the quantum dynamics of the meter system allows us to identify a universal relation between quantum interference in the post-selection probability, and quantum interference in the statistics of the meter readout. The analysis reveals that quantum interference modifies the readout distribution of the meter in two ways, a diffusion term that identifies the appropriate operator ordering in the post-selected variance of the observed system property, and a wavefunction-dependent update of the initial meter statistics based on the effect of back action on the post-selection probability. Our results show that the statistical patterns described by meter interference provide important details about the physics of post-selection in weak measurements, allowing us to exclude the possibility of statistical artefacts in the experimental observation of weak values.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how interference patterns in the readout statistics of a meter used in a weak measurement can reveal information about the system's underlying quantum properties. By relating interference terms in the post-selection probability to fluctuations in the meter reading, the authors demonstrate that these statistical details allow for the objective determination of weak values. This provides a rigorous framework for interpreting measurements where standard assumptions about classical statistics break down.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum interference effects, specifically those arising from meter readout statistics, can reveal fundamental details about weak measurements.
main_result: It establishes a universal relationship between quantum interference in the post-selection probability and the interference observed in the meter readout statistics. This analysis shows that these interference terms correct for measurement fluctuations, allowing objective values to be determined by weak values.
method: The authors perform a careful theoretical analysis of the quantum dynamics of an interacting system (the observable) and a continuous variable meter during post-selection. They utilize quasi-probability distributions to track interference effects.
model_or_system: The model involves a general weak measurement setup where a system observable $\hat{A}$ interacts unitarily with a meter whose position is continuously measured. The analysis focuses on the resulting joint probability distribution $P(f, x)$ after post-selection ($f$).
key_observables: Quantum interference in the post-selection probability; quantum interference in the meter readout statistics; weak values ($\langle A \rangle_w$); conditional fluctuations (e.g., Ozawa-Hall uncertainty).
important_parameters: Measurement strength ($s$), which dictates whether the measurement is weak or projective.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that quantum interference effects are measurable in the meter readout statistics and that these statistics provide more information than just conditional averages.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework by analyzing the joint probability of post-selection and meter readout. It then details how interference terms modify both the average value and, crucially, the conditional fluctuations (variance) observed in the meter.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical understanding of measurement contextuality and weak measurements, which is highly relevant for quantum optics and open quantum systems where continuous monitoring or weak coupling is central to the physics.
